steps.text: Pour ½ cup room temperature water into a small bowl; sprinkle yeast over water and let stand to dissolve, about 5 minutes.

Combine white sugar, shortening, and salt in a large bowl; pour 1 cup boiling water over shortening mixture, then stir in evaporated milk. Cool mixture until lukewarm, then add yeast mixture and beaten eggs.
Slowly mix in flour until dough forms a ball. Cover dough with plastic wrap and refrigerate 30 to 60 minutes.

Roll out dough, working with a small portion (a little larger than a baseball) at a time, until ⅛-inch thick. Cut dough into strips 2- to 3-inches wide, then cut at an angle in the opposite direction, making diamond shapes.
Heat oil in a deep, wide, heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat to 360 degrees F (180 degrees C).

Lower dough diamonds carefully into the hot oil in batches. Fry until puffed and golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Carefully transfer to a rack set on paper towels to drain; cool until you can handle them.
Place beignets in a clean paper bag with confectioners' sugar; shake gently until covered generously. Or use a sifter to dust beignets with confectioners' sugar.

raw_recipe.description: Try this genuine recipe for Costas French Market doughnuts (beignets). These tender pillow-like doughnuts taste like those at New Orleans' Cafe du Monde.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make traditional fluffy beignets like they serve at New Orleans’ famous Café du Monde. Enjoyed with a cup of coffee, these pillow-like, powdered sugar-coated donuts are the perfect way to wake up.

review.reviewBody: These little gems are not Cafe Du Mond quality but darn close. I think the dough is missing a little something. I think I might try adding some vanilla or almond extract on my next go around. A couple of modifications I made to this recipe was to use peanut oil rather than the vegtable oil and for the topping, add a little cinnamon and pumpkin pie spice to the powdered sugar. I highly recommend giving it a try!

These were awesome! I am a fan of using my breadmaker so I mixed the sugar, shortening (except I used margarine instead because I was out of shortening), boiled water, etc... and the extra water you are supposed to dissolve the yeast in all together and then the flour on top and the yeast on top of that and set my breadmaker on the dough cycle. When it had 30 minutes left I popped the dough in the fridge for the last 30mins. They came out to be perfect little pillows of deliciousness!

Delicious. I am a private chef and had these requested by a client...They turned out amazing. Very tasty, and airy. I actually let the dough sit in the fridge overnight and punched it down once. I took the advice of others and added vanilla bean. As another reviewer mentioned, make sure you use the right amount of yeast. The recipe calls for a tablespoon, and one packet of dry yeast in only 2.25 teaspoons. 

I also froze a bunch of cut out beignets and put them in layers on parchment paper. I cooked them up this morning and turned out just as good as the first time. Thanks for the great recipe.

These were awesome and they make a lot! Yay, more for me and guests! I did add vanilla as others suggested. The only other change was that I let it rise after cutting and before frying. This allowed them to puff up even better and get nice and soft. So those that might have had bricks, that might have been the reason. I keep a stash now in the freezer in case company pops in unannounced.

This rating is for this recipe as BREAD. I refrigerated it overnight, brought it to room temperature, divided it into two loaves, kneaded them slightly to form loaves to fit loaf pans sprayed with cooking spray, covered them with a towel, then let them rest in the oven for about an hour. After than time, remove the towels, set the oven temperature to 350 (without preheating) and bake for 50 minutes. The dough rises even more and bakes perfectly. A light crunchy crust and a moist, even center. Very clean taste. Totally delicious. Great as is or toasted.

These were a success the FIRST time I made them:-) I followed recipe exactly except I added 1/2 tsp almond extract to dough. Read recipe before starting to be sure you have enough flour! (I used about 6 1/4 cups). Cut them in small triangles (size of index finger-max), and drop only 3 at a time in hot oil to be certain they don't get over-browned. (Be sure temp of oil is correct too).
 I tossed in a grocery paper bag when done and dumped 1 c. powdered sugar on top then shook closed bag.
I served with sliced strawberries + whipped cream in a dessert bowl with a Beignet on top. Classy and yummy !

These were really good! I did make the addition of 1 Tbsp vanilla and 1 Tbsp cinnamon to the dough, and it sat closer to 2 hours in the fridge. I also free-handed circles instead of rolling and cutting. Everyone really enjoyed them and said that they were fantastic, but would be even better filled! Will definitely reccommend adding the vanilla and cinnamon, or else this would have been a 2 star recipe for blandness. Very good recipe for my first ever doughnuts.

Excellent dough. I stirred by hand it is IMPOSSIBLE to 7.5 cups of flour (I tried twice and the first batch was ruined). So I ended up using 6 cups and it was still delicious. I ended up cooking at 325º for a longer time until golden brown, supper fluffy inside! Thanks for a great recipe!

Added sprinkling of sugar to yeast mixture, didn't wait for liquids to cool all the way and added extra sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg. Waited for the yeast mixture for 10-15 minutes, let the dough rest for 1 hour in the fridge. 

Tested one in the fryer, when ready they should rise quickly and puff up very fast. We had to turn down the temperature because they were ready too fast. The perfect color for these seems to be a light golden brown. 6-8 seconds on each side in our fryer. After they were done we let them cool for a few seconds and then when they were cool enough to handle we dipped them in melted chocolate. They were delicious, and we are all very full. We will be making these again (and not just because there is a huge amount of dough left.)

I made these for my family and they were a hit. The first time i made them they were not that sweet so the second time i made them, i used 1 cup of sugar and they were sweet enough that they didnt even need the dusted powdered sugar. I also didnt have evaporated milk so i used regular whole milk which turned out fine. Also, the second time i made them i used coconut milk instead which gave them a nice coco-nutty taste. The original recipe makes alot of beignets so i used half the dough and froze the other half for later use, although i ended up making them again the very next day because my kids ate them all up and kept asking for more.

I've used this recipe to see how it stood against my grandmother's recipe and have to say it holds up. Next week I'll do a favorite here with the kids now crawfish (to you that are not from here crayfish) is coming into season making a crawfish etouffee with out rice and stuff into the beignet and top with more. Or stuff the beignet with a crawfish crab mixture using polenta (grits) and top with the etouffee.
This is the best recipe i love it
Easy to make. My kids love it. One of my faves that I share with my friends.

Well i made the dough Saturday But officially made them a while ago ... Absolutely wonderful .. a very simple recipe most ingredients always in your home. I added a little mixed essence too! but next time gonna add raisins not to many just a few ....
i decided to make these and followed the recipe to a T, well, they came out dry and tasteless, all i could taste was the shortening,
I made these to celebrate my birthday and pretend I was at Disney, two hearty thumbs up. I made a 1/2 recipe, it was easy and they turned out perfectly!
I was nervous to make this. I’m not exoeoeiemced making dough. This was the easiest dough to make. And it turned out perfectly. Thank you!

They were delicious! However, if giving half stars were an option I would give these a 4 1/2 star rating. The inside was a little bit airy, but it also complimented it too. I would definitely make it again!
Great recipe! Easy to follow and yummy to eat. Thanks so much!
Great Recipe! Made during the COVID-19 quarantine. These tasted amazing and my family loved them. Will make again!
